title: Leadership team assessment tools: what to look for
description: Eight checks for choosing a leadership team assessment tool, and how {product} meets each: anonymity, timing, agreement, evidence and action.
h1: How to choose a leadership team assessment tool
lead: {product} is a research-based tool for assessing and improving a leadership team of 4 to 15 people, starting with a free three-minute scan. Whichever tool you choose, check the eight points below before you ask your team to answer.

head: Check
Why it matters
How {product} does it
rows: It measures the team, not individuals
When a team survey rates people, members answer to protect themselves.
Questions ask about the team, and no result is shown per person.
Anonymity is enforced, not promised
In a group of four to fifteen, a promise is easy to break by accident.
A threshold of four answers, held in the database and never lowered. Counts only, never names.
Nothing shows before the close
Early results shape later answers, and show who answered when.
Results open when the round closes, and are computed once.
It shows agreement, not only averages
A middling average can hide a team that is split.
Every theme shows its level and an agreement label.
The research is visible
Research-based should be something you can check.
Each scale names its layer and its evidence rating.
It is honest about its own evidence
Evidence for the ideas is not evidence for the questionnaire.
Every score says Research-based, not yet validated.
It leads to action
Results that stay in a report change little.
Focus areas with actions that appear on the next agenda.
You can start alone
A first reading should not wait for a workshop.
The scan is free, takes about three minutes and needs no account.

items: Who can see individual answers, including your own staff?
What is the smallest number of answers a result needs, and who can change it?
Can results be filtered by role, location or tenure? In a small team, that can identify someone.
What evidence is there for the questionnaire itself, not only for the ideas behind it?
Where is the data kept, and what leaves the tool?

blocks.text: A tool gives the team a shared picture. Some teams read it together without help; others benefit from a coach or facilitator, especially when views differ sharply or trust is low. A good tool makes either way possible.
What should you read before you choose?

Start with [how to assess a leadership team](/articles/how-to-assess-a-leadership-team), which covers methods, questions and pitfalls. Then read [what makes a leadership team effective](/articles/what-makes-a-leadership-team-effective) for the research behind the questions.

faq.q: What is a leadership team assessment?
faq.a: A structured way to see how a leadership team works: its conditions, how it meets and decides, and the trust and safety between members. Usually every member answers the same questions anonymously.

faq.q: How many members need to answer?
faq.a: In {product}, at least four. Below that, no team result is shown, because a result for three or fewer can point to one person.

faq.q: How often should a leadership team be assessed?
faq.a: A full reading once or twice a year, with short pulses between, works for most teams. In {product}, the Full diagnostic gives the full reading, and pulses follow your focus areas between.
